items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: I would have not agreed, if I had kept him, to let Joe Carroll go. Because Joe Carroll was an asset to him.

ctx.x: he made so much noise over there as a single. He had a great group. He had this boy Joe in there, that did the singing...

Yeah. Dizzy was a good comedian, so... I got involved with that a little bit when Snooky was on 45th Street or 44th Street, and that's how I got close to Dizzy. Because I got him the job down there... Because I was having trouble with Morris Levy. Morris Levy didn't want to pay him more... We was trying to make another fifty dollars. We was only making twelve-hundred dollars; we was trying to get $1250 -- and he just didn't want to pay us no more money. So I went and got him a job for $1500 at Snooky's. And he…
